author: BrianLYS
order: Commit version and native build-tool preparation.
Publish BendHub anonymously with the pinned compiler and verify the downloaded package.
Commit the hash/manifest, updated consumer pins and verification evidence.
Build and verify a clean archive from that exact candidate; push main and wait for both CI workflows.
Tag the verified candidate, publish the pre-release, then download and compare both assets.
Record publication and final CI results in a subsequent documentation/evidence commit.
why: BendHub precedes tagging so the immutable tag includes its verified hash and matching manifest. Consumer pins name an earlier immutable 0.3.0 source/native-tool anchor with matching bytes, avoiding a circular self-referential Git hash. The archive manifest names the exact tagged commit. Publication receipts are committed afterwards without changing that tag.
limits: Independent Lean/BendTT kernel verification is not claimed.
Native prebuilt archive is macOS arm64 only; other platforms build from source.
Historical workload measurements retain their original revisions.
